meta.title: Parallelize workflow checks
meta.body_summary: Speed up CI feedback by parallelizing steps in test.yml; later closed as experimental by the author.

perf_labels.notes: Codex-generated CI refactoring closed by author due to poor prompt; no formal review, no benchmark, and no evidence of performance gain.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 198 changed lines in a single CI workflow file, this is a small refactor by absolute volume. As a CI speed-up experiment it was closed without merge; author self-evaluated the split as insufficient and chose not to pursue it.

review_details.concern_detail: Author noted the prompt needs to be more elaborate to achieve a proper split into code and non-code checks, and later closed without further work.
review_details.performance_claim: Parallelization speeds up CI feedback by running checks concurrently.
review_details.rejection_signals: Author self-closed; no external review; deemed experimental with insufficient prompt quality.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Codex-generated CI parallelization works syntactically but lacks domain-specific prompt refinement to achieve a meaningful split between code and non-code checks; author abandoned due to prompt complexity.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No CI run time data or benchmarks; only author's comment about prompt inadequacy.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: PR closed without further work; no regression testing.

core_change_summary.description: In .github/workflows/test.yml, reorganized job steps into parallel groups, adding 'source checks' steps and adjusting dependencies to reduce CI runtime.
change_trajectory: Initial commit: parallelize test workflow by splitting steps.
Second commit: add steps for source checks.
Author commented on prompt inadequacy; PR closed after 9 days.

review_signals.summary: Author states the PR was created for fun, prompt needs more elaboration to achieve a proper split between code and non-code checks.
Not planning to work on this CODEX generated PR.
